newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Foreign workers edge out Arabs for jobs in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Foreign workers edge out Arabs for jobs in Israel.

text.p: Thousands of Palestinians allowed to cross from the West Bank and Gaza Strip for work in Israel fail to find jobs in the Jewish state due to competition from Asian and Eastern European workers, officials said on Tuesday.
The Israeli and PLO officials said Israeli employers preferred to hire foreign workers because Palestinians were subject to frequent Israeli closures which prevented them from reaching their jobs.
Only about 70 percent of Palestinian permit-holders were making use of them.

"Palestinian workers have not used all their quotas because as a result of frequent closures which ban entry of workers to Israel, Israeli employers fire their Palestinian workers," said Sa'id Mudallal, director-general of the Palestinian labour ministry.
"Another reason is the lack of job opportunities in Israel since foreign labour replaced Palestinian workers," he told Reuters.
He said 65,000 residents of the West Bank and Gaza Strip were holding permits to work in Israel but only about 46,000 of them crossed into the Jewish state for work every day.

The director-general of Israel's labour and social affairs minstry confirmed the trend and said Israel aimed to gradually reduce the number of Asians and Eastern Europeans working in Israel and increase the number of permits given to Palestinians.
"We hope within four years to reduce the number of foreign workers from 100,000 to 25,000 and raise the number of Palestinians working in Israel to 80,000," Yigal Ben-Shalom said.
Israel imposed a ban on the entry of Palestinians to Israel after a wave of suicide bombings last year by Moslem militants which killed 59 people in the Jewish state.

The closure has been gradually eased but is occasionally reimposed to prevent Palestinians from carrying out attacks in Israel. The Palestinian self-rule Authority has repeatedly urged Israel to let more Palestinians work in the Jewish state.
Under current Israeli criteria, only Palestinians over 28 years of age and married are allowed to work in the Jewish state.
Palestinians say the periodic ban amounts to collective punishment and has ravaged the economy in the West Bank and Gaza.
Israeli authorities began in 1993 giving Asians and Eastern Europeans permits to work in Israel. At the time, about 85,000 Palestinians had jobs in Israel.
Mudallal said he asked Israeli officials to give permits to Palestinian workers under 25-years-old to ease unemployment in the West Bank and Gaza.

According to a study conducted by the Palestinian Monetary Authority based on data from the Palestinian Statistics Department, unemployment has reached around 60 percent in the Gaza Strip and 38 percent in the West Bank.
